name: Microscaling Data Formats for Deep Learning
authors: Rouhani, David, Nic, Tutus, Awwad, Khorzad, Bhandari, Garg
problem: Narrow formats force a choice between hardware efficiency and accuracy, and per-tensor scales are too coarse for weights and gradients that vary wildly element to element.
mechanism: Defines the OCP Microscaling (MX) family: a shared power-of-two scale per fixed 32-element block plus a narrow element format (E2M1/E3M2/E4M3/E5M2 for floats, E8M0 for the shared scale). The shared block scale is what makes the format hardware-friendly - one scale for 32 elements amortizes the scale-fetch cost to near nothing - and the choice of block size 32 is a hardware decision, not an accuracy one. Evaluated as a drop-in FP32 replacement across two dozen benchmarks.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): MX formats are a practical drop-in replacement for FP32 for inference and training with low user friction, evaluated over two dozen benchmarks, plus the FIRST instance of training generative language models at sub-8-bit weights, activations AND gradients with minimal accuracy loss and no modification to the training recipe. COMPRESSION RATIO: with the shared scale, 8-bit elements land near 8.3 bits/weight and 4-bit elements near 4.25 bits/weight - the block scale is overhead, not savings. QUALITY COST: 'minimal accuracy loss' for the sub-8-bit training result; the exact per-benchmark deltas are in the paper's tables, not the abstract.
